name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Eric Burlison running with large financial edge
Minimal Democratic fundraising and no outside spending
model.rationale: Burlison holds a heavily Republican southwest Missouri seat with a roughly 20-point structural lean, a large cash advantage, and no serious outside opposition, while Hesketh has raised little. Prediction markets price a Republican win near 96%, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major scandal or an unexpectedly strong Democratic wave environment could narrow the margin, though a seat this red is unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Missouri's seventh district is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Eric Burlison was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with roughly $960,000 on hand, having raised nearly $1.5 million. Democratic challenger Missi Hesketh has raised only about $50,000, and no outside groups are spending in the race. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Burlison about a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican victory in the mid-to-high teens, with little evidence suggesting a competitive contest.
